# CRM Industry Core Conclusions

| Dimension | Current knowledge |
| --- | --- |
| Industry role | CRM is the system of record for customer identity, relationships, marketing, sales, service, channel collaboration and revenue analysis. It is broader than a contact directory or a lead list. |
| Best-fit demand | High-value B2B sales with long cycles, repeated follow-up, complex quotations and a need to connect ERP, finance or order data. |
| Priority segments | Export manufacturing, industrial distribution and cross-border B2B are the first priority segments; B2B software/services and international logistics are secondary segments. |
| Market stage | CRM is moving from customer records and sales-process digitisation toward unified data, AI-assisted decisions and AI-executed workflows. |
| Data boundary | Industry economic indicators are proxy indicators for the customer pool, not CRM SaaS TAM. CRM, CRM SaaS and sales-force-automation figures use different statistical scopes. |
| Compliance baseline | Customer data, marketing outreach, profiling, AI-generated content and cross-border transfers require purpose limitation, permissions, consent or another lawful basis, auditability and user controls. |
| Durable opportunity | Industry workflows, AI execution, quotation/order/collection linkage, data quality, compliant cross-border outreach and low-complexity deployment are more defensible than an AI label alone. |
